title: Coefficient sections over pro-étale objects agree with global sections after pullback
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme and use its small pro-étale site and universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ the coefficient ring on each scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an object $u:V\to B$ of $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the forgetful functor identifies $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the localized site $(B_{\mathrm{proét}})/V$: objects are $W\to V$ and coverings are the same families of weakly étale maps. Under this identification, the abelian inverse image $u^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is restriction to that localized site. With the canonical coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_u:u^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}\Lambda_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], evaluation at the final object $V\to V$ gives a ring isomorphism
$$\theta_V:\Lambda_B(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V).$$

For every $B$-morphism $h:W\to V$ between objects of $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $s\in\Lambda_B(V)$, these isomorphisms satisfy
$$h^\sharp(\theta_V(s))=\theta_W(\Lambda_B(h)(s)).$$
Here $h^\sharp$ is the section map $r\mapsto\alpha_h\circ h^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}r$ after the monoidal-unit identification, and $\Lambda_B(h)$ is ordinary sheaf restriction. If $m_{\theta_V(s)}$ denotes the endomorphism of the regular $\Lambda_V$-module given by multiplication by $\theta_V(s)$, then the module pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], under $h^*\Lambda_V\cong\Lambda_W$, sends it to $m_{\theta_W(\Lambda_B(h)(s))}$.

Apply to the weakly étale small pro-étale sites; compare proetale.tex Tag 098T (lemma-morphism-big-small). Compatibility with the specific condensed coefficient maps alpha is an agent-formulated ringed specialization, using sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp.

proof.text: Use weaklyEtale_localization for the explicit slice equivalence and covering equations. The composition/base-change adjunction gives localizationRestriction left adjoint to lowerStar. Uniqueness of left adjoints supplies upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction for the very upperStar in the statement; no comparison of independently constructed inverse-image functors is needed.

For V over B let k be the isomorphism from the composition of V/V with V to the object V/B. The diagonal graph is the site-adjunction unit followed by base change of k. Naturality therefore factors the stated theta as F(k) followed by the restriction-adjunction mate of eta at V/V. Uniqueness of adjoints identifies that mate with the inverse comparison followed by alpha. Both factors are isomorphisms.

Apply the unit and multiplication equations of the actual coefficient mate. Evaluation through sheafToPresheaf, compatibility of epsilon and mu with continuous direct image, and naturality along the graph give exactly the stated unit and product identities. The canonical coefficient unit and multiplication maps are concrete transported morphisms. Proved formula lemmas explicitly rewrite the coefficient operations and section map before applying these generic identities.

First naturality of eta along h identifies ordinary restriction followed by theta_W with eta for W/B at V/B restricted along the graph (h,id). Next the pullback-composition isomorphism sends the graph of a composite to the base-changed graph composed with the global graph. Verify this by the two pullback projections. Naturality of eta_h and the eta composition law then identify theta_V followed by h-sharp with the same map. This retains both diagonal and graph, and works without a monomorphism assumption.

For a global section r define a sectionwise endomorphism of the regular module by multiplication with its restriction to each test object. Ring restriction maps make it natural and commutativity makes every component linear. Full faithfulness of the internal-to-sectionwise module functor gives an actual internal module morphism, with the prescribed component formula definitionally.

For a monoid-sheaf map eta:R to f_*S, its evaluated ring homomorphism preserves products. Naturality along the final arrow identifies the image of the restricted global section with the restriction of its global graph image. Consequently m_r followed by eta equals eta followed by f_*m_(f-sharp r), componentwise. Applying the upperStar/lowerStar Hom equivalence transfers this identity to upperStar(m_r) followed by alpha equals alpha followed by m_(f-sharp r).

For an isomorphism of monoid objects alpha:R to S, the identity underlying S gives regularIsoComapRegular. Transpose its hom through extendHomEquiv to define q. Since comap along an isomorphism is an equivalence, extendScalars and its adjunction unit are equivalences/isomorphisms; the triangle identity and reflection of isomorphisms show q is invertible. extendUnitHom_extendHom gives the exact normalization. Injectivity of the same adjunction Hom equivalence proves that q intertwines any compatible endomorphisms. Apply this to the mapped regular module and the multiplication identity from the previous step, then use theta naturality.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00Y0, 03CE, 03EH and 00YV; X2 Lean proof uses canonical adjoint uniqueness, the eta composition law, sectionwise internal-module full faithfulness, and the existing extension-restriction adjunction rather than a separate Kan or pure-tensor computation.
